explanation:
## How the puzzle works

**What the grid is made of.** Each input has four coloured shapes arranged around one empty background cell, which I'll call the centre. One shape sits above the centre, one below, one left and one right. Each shape has a single **tip cell** that points at the centre: it is the first non-background cell you reach when you walk from the centre in that direction.

- Pair 1: the centre is (8,7). The tips are 4 at (7,7), 7 at (9,7), 2 at (8,5) and 9 at (8,9).
- Pairs 2 and 3 have the same centre and the same four tip positions.

**What changes.** Exactly 6 cells change in every pair:

1. Three of the four tips become background.
2. The fourth shape keeps its tip. It also gains 3 cells, added as a line just beyond its far edge, centred on the centre's row or column.
   - Pair 1: shape 4 (above the centre, rows 2–7) gains row y=1 at x=6..8.
   - Pair 2: shape 7 (right of the centre, columns 9–11) gains column x=12 at y=7..9.
   - Pair 3: shape 3 (above the centre) gains row y=2 at x=6..8.

It reads as the winner taking the three tips the losers gave up and stacking them on its back.

**Who wins.** The winner always has the most cells of its colour:
- Pair 1: 4 has 16 cells; the others have 13, 4 and 3.
- Pair 2: 7 has 9 cells; the others have 8, 8 and 4.
- Pair 3: 3 has 22 cells; the others have 16, 14 and 7.

**Finding the centre in code.** I scan every background cell and cast rays up, down, left and right. A valid centre is one whose four rays hit four different colours. Among valid centres I pick the one with the smallest total ray length.

**Test input.** The centre is (7,7). The rays hit 9 above, 1 below, 6 on the left and 2 on the right, each at distance 2. The largest colour is 9 with 19 cells (2 has 18), so 9 wins:
- The tips 6 at (7,5), 2 at (7,9) and 1 at (9,7) are cleared.
- The 9 shape spans rows 2–5, so it gains a row of 9s at y=1, x=6..8.

**Teaching stages.** The program emits two checkpoints: one after clearing the three losing tips, and one after stamping the 3-cell line onto the winner (the final grid).
